surface_mechanism_description: Growth rate decreased with increase in N2 plasma exposure time due to effective removal of carbon-containing ligands from TMI, leading to self-limiting growth. The reaction becomes self-terminating with sufficient TMI exposure, and growth-per-cycle (GPC) shows saturation behavior. The presence of carbon ligands from TMI was attributed to incomplete reaction with N2 plasma, and longer N2 plasma exposure time helped in removing these ligands, decreasing the growth rate.
evidence: During optimization experiments, N2 plasma flow rate and plasma power were kept constant as 50 sccm and 300W, respectively. Growth rate decreases progressively with increase in N2 plasma exposure time from 40 s to 100 s. It was found as 1.60 Å/cycle with 40 s of plasma exposure time which decreases to 0.64 Å/cycle under 100 s of exposure time. XPS measurements revealed a decrease in carbon content of the films with increase in N2 plasma exposure time. Previously, we have demonstrated HCPA-ALD of AlN, BN, and GaN films using the trimethylaluminum, triethylboron, and trimethylgallium, respectively together with N2/H2 plasma. These metal precursors belong to the organometallic precursor family which contains methyl/ethyl groups bonded to metal atoms. Purpose of using H2 plasma in addition to N2 plasma was to effectively remove the carbon ligands during the film growth.
